physics-h1-q1.material: Near the Earth's surface, of two steel balls A and B at the same height, A is released from rest to fall freely, and B is launched forcefully in the horizontal direction. Which statement about their motion is correct? (Ignore air resistance.)
physics-h1-q1.thinking.0: Simultaneous Fall of Projectiles and Free-Falling Bodies
physics-h1-q1.s.s1.prompt: Near the Earth's surface, of two steel balls A and B at the same height, A is released from rest to fall freely, and B is launched forcefully in the horizontal direction. Which statement about their motion is correct? (Ignore air resistance.)

physics-h1-q2.topic: Collision Duration and Impact Force Reduction (I = FΔt)
physics-h1-q2.goal: វិភាគគោលការណ៍នៃ Collision Duration and Impact Force Reduction (I = FΔt) និងទាញការសន្និដ្ឋានត្រឹមត្រូវតាមលក្ខខណ្ឌដែលបានកំណត់។
physics-h1-q2.material: Two eggs of the same mass are dropped from the same height, one onto a cement floor and the other onto a soft cushion. Which comparison of physical quantities, from the moment each egg touches the surface until it stops, is correct?
physics-h1-q2.thinking.0: Collision Duration and Impact Force Reduction (I = FΔt)
physics-h1-q2.s.s1.prompt: Two eggs of the same mass are dropped from the same height, one onto a cement floor and the other onto a soft cushion. Which comparison of physical quantities, from the moment each egg touches the surface until it stops, is correct?
physics-h1-q2.s.s1.explain: Because the change in momentum ($\Delta p$) of the two eggs is the same, the impulse ($I = F\Delta t$) is identical. The cushion lengthens the collision time $\Delta t$, reducing the average impact force $F = \frac{I}{\Delta t}$, so the egg does not break.
physics-h1-q2.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
physics-h1-q2.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
physics-h1-q2.s.s1.hint.0: Since they fall from the same height, the velocity just before impact and the velocity change to rest (change in momentum = impulse) are the same.
physics-h1-q2.s.s1.hint.1: The soft cushion deforms and lengthens the collision time (Δt).
physics-h1-q2.s.s2.hint.0: Recall the cause-effect relationships established in the first step.
physics-h1-q2.s.s1.o.o0: The magnitude of the impulse is the same, but the average force on the egg on the cushion is smaller
physics-h1-q2.s.s1.o.o1: The impulse on the egg on the cushion is smaller
physics-h1-q2.s.s1.o.o2: The collision time of the egg dropped on the cement floor is longer

physics-h1-q3.thinking.0: Baseball Hits, Impulse, and Momentum Change
physics-h1-q3.s.s1.prompt: A baseball of mass 0.5 kg is traveling at 30 m/s when it is hit by a bat and bounces back in the opposite direction at 40 m/s. What is the magnitude of the impulse the ball received?

physics-h1-q3.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.

physics-h1-c.thinking.0: Horizontal Cliff Launch Trajectory and Flight Time
physics-h1-c.s.s1.prompt: [Advanced mechanics] An object of mass 1 kg is launched horizontally at 20 m/s from the edge of an 80 m high cliff. How far does it travel horizontally before reaching the ground? (Use g = 10 m/s² and ignore air resistance.)
physics-h1-c.s.s1.explain: The vertical fall time is $80 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2 \implies t^2 = 16 \implies t = 4$ s. Since horizontal motion is uniform, the horizontal distance is $x = v_x t = 20\text{ m/s} \times 4\text{ s} = 80\text{ m}$.
physics-h1-c.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
physics-h1-c.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
